newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest spot power falls along with natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest spot power falls along with natgas.

text.p: Wholesale spot electricity prices for the U.S. Mid-West mostly fell Monday along with a drop in spot natural gas prices, industry sources said.
Temperatures through much of the Mid-West were expected to be near normal levels through this week, with some milder temperatures expected by the weekend in the Southwest Power Pool (SPP).
Also, Detroit Edison will interrupt the restart of its 1,116 megawatt Fermi 2 nuclear power plant for several days of repairs.
The plant had begun the restart process from scheduled maintenance but an electronic problem will postpone output for "a matter of days," the company said.
In the Mid-Continent Area Power Pool (MAPP), peak non-firm power deals for Tuesday delivery were pegged steady at $25.00-27.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Business in MAPP was said to be thin with few buyers interested in purchasing for that price, sources said.
Off-peak non-firm MAPP power deals were notionally pegged steady in the $12.00-14.00 range, the sources said.
In the Mid-American Interpool Network (MAIN) peak, non-firm power for Tuesday delivery was pegged steady to lower at $21.00-25.00 from $23.00-25.00 late last week.
MAIN off peak power was said to be steady at $12.00-14.00.

Peak, non-firm electricity prices in the East Central Area Reliability Coordination Agreement (ECAR) for Tuesday delivery were assessed at $19.00-22.00 from $22.00-23.00 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day ECAR power was notionally assessed steady at $13.00-15.00.
In SPP, peak non-firm power prices for Tuesday delivery were talked lower at $20.00-22.00 from $26.00-27.50 late last week, the sources said.
Off-peak prices throughout SPP were notionally said to be steady in the $13.00-15.00 area.
January/February peak SPP power was pegged lower at $25.75-26.25 per MWh from $27.00-27.50 late last week, the sources said.
